Neither variant carries a site for any Golden Gate enzyme - BsaI, BsmBI/Esp3I, BbsI/BpiI, SapI, AarI/PaqCI, BtgZI, BspQI all clean on both, checked against Biopython's REBASE set. The EMMA codon differences are not domestication; nothing needed removing. The enzymes that do differ between the two are obscure non-cloning ones (BslI family and several homing-type).

The EMMA part itself is Golden Gate: it is an Esp3I-flanked level-0 part, overhangs CCAG and GCTG. That is the same enzyme Fragmid uses as its shuttle, so an EMMA part cannot be dropped into a Fragmid Esp3I reaction without the two conflicting.

All six vectors put GAC (Asp) at +1, immediately after the leader's Gly, despite completely different downstream content. Asp is the native +1 residue of the mouse kappa light chain, so every designer kept the natural cleavage context. See igk_leader_plus1.tsv.

Near-misses are not worth screening. Across 48.8 kb of real vector DNA (the six maps plus p003 and p008), BsaI/Esp3I/BbsI give 30 exact sites and 1,239 sequences one base away - 25.4 near-misses per kb against 0.61 real sites per kb, a 41-fold excess. p003 alone carries 301. Recoding near-misses would mean recoding almost everything, which is the opposite of the native-codon-usage rule in Fragmid 4.2.

What does matter is junction completion: two clean sequences can make a site at the seam where they meet. That is already the rule for barcodes in S4E9 - a barcode clean in isolation can still complete a site against its flanks - and the same check belongs on the leader-to-receptor fusion, which is 25 new seams the library has never had. Deterministic and cheap, since both flanks are known.

EMMA publishes no guidance on this. The Addgene kit page gives no part-standardisation procedure and names no enzyme; the paper is paywalled with no PMC copy. The enzyme was read off the part itself rather than the docs: 100697 is Esp3I-flanked with overhangs CCAG and GCTG.
